fields.title: Internal view: what the company can and cannot actually do
fields.keyTakeaway: A core strength is proven by outcomes and hard to replicate, not just an internal self-image. Almost every strength imposes a constraint: it defines what you explicitly choose not to do.
fields.checkQuestion: "Our strength is a strong engineering team." How do you verify if that is true?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key node question: **what internal capabilities and constraints exist?**
fields.blocks/1/subtitle: It usually turns into four lists of compliments — here is how to avoid that
fields.blocks/1/items/0: **Strengths** — strictly backed by evidence: repeatable results others fail to match. "We deploy in three days vs. two weeks for competitors" — yes; "customer focus" — no.
fields.blocks/1/items/1: **Weaknesses** — facts hurting performance right now: lead times, churn, unit cost.
fields.blocks/1/items/2: **Opportunities and threats** — external factors, building on the previous lesson.
fields.blocks/1/items/3: **The key is intersections:** which strength captures an opportunity, which weakness exposes you to a threat. The value of SWOT lies entirely in these pairs.
fields.blocks/2/text: **Company lifecycle stage** clarifies decisions that might look nonsensical on the surface. A young startup relies on brute-force sales and key individuals; a scale-up drowns in missing process; a mature company defends turf and moves slowly. Demanding enterprise order from a fast-growing company is asking for the impossible.
fields.blocks/3/text:
Strength: 3-day implementation vs 2 weeks for a major competitor. Evidence: 34 onboardings last year, averaging 3.4 days.
Weakness: missing integrations with two popular ERPs; caused 11 lost deals out of 27 unclosed ones over the year.
Opportunity: mandatory product labeling effective September 1 — all clients must upgrade.
Threat: major competitor announced a cloud version at half our price.

Actionable intersection: deployment speed + mandatory labeling = we can convert customers before September while the competitor takes two weeks per setup. This became our H2 strategic priority.

Second intersection: missing integrations + low-cost competitor = whenever a deal degrades into price comparison, we lose twice as fast.
fields.blocks/4/text: Fast customer support becomes a competitive advantage only if rivals cannot match it due to structural reasons: different sales model, scale, or SLAs. Otherwise, it is just a temporary state.
fields.blocks/4/title: Easily copied strengths are not true advantages
fields.blocks/5/text: SWOT does not prioritize initiatives or compare options. It simply synthesizes the picture prior to decision-making; the decision itself relies on finances and trade-offs.
